Blocks.Text: As a LinkedIn partner, a customer application represents your customer's unique instance within your ATS that connects to LinkedIn's APIs. You have to create a customer application for each customer. Each application has its own API key and configuration settings that control how their jobs and applicants are managed through the Apply Connect integration.
Important

Access to this API is restricted to approved developers. Contact your LinkedIn Relationship Manager or Business Development representative to discuss criteria and sign the required API agreement with data restrictions. If you are not yet a LinkedIn Talent Solutions Partner, complete the LinkedIn Talent Solutions Partner Request Form.
Take the following steps to create and configure customer applications.

Provision customers
Create enablement toggle
Display the ATS integration configuration plugin
Sync customer integration

Use the Provisioning API to create API keys for customers. Store a unique API key and LinkedIn Developer Application ID for each customer. If your customer already has API keys from other LinkedIn integrations (Job Postings, Recruiter System Connect, or Apply with LinkedIn), reuse those existing keys. Refer to complete configuration details.
Note
All API requests require authorization.
Take the following actions to create the enablement toggle:

Provide a toggle in your application settings that allows customers to enable or disable LinkedIn Easy Apply at both the account level and individual job level.
Display the following required text directly next to or below the toggle in a noticeable font size and color: "By posting your job to LinkedIn, you agree to LinkedIn's Jobs Terms & Conditions. Learn more about using LinkedIn Easy Apply".
Important
By default, customers should be opted in to LinkedIn Easy Apply and the toggle should be readily available in an appropriate location within your settings.

Blocks.Text: Display the ATS Integration configuration plugin to allow LinkedIn Recruiter customers to enable Apply Connect features— Profile Plugin and Applicant Notifications. Embed this widget code in your ATS where customers manage their integration or job board settings.

Blocks.Text: Use the ATS Onboarding widget to capture customer integration details. Prefill the integrationContext input field with the value from the Onboarding widget callback response, then sync this data back to /atsIntegrations.

SectionPath: Step 3: Display ATS integration configuration plugin
Blocks.Text: The plugin will load based on the data-width and data-supported-bundled-integration-types attributes you specify. Use the latter attribute to declare which integrations you support.
After a customer configures their integration, make a sync request to the following endpoint with the provided values.
POST https://api.linkedin.com/v2/atsIntegrations?ids[0].integrationContext={integrationContext}&ids[0].integrationType={integrationType}&ids[0].tenantType={tenantType}&ids[0].dataProvider=ATS
Note
Create integrations from your server (not client-side) immediately when the customer completes the Onboarding widget flow.
Submit batch calls with no more than 100 records per batch and a minimum one-second delay between calls. Use the following values from the Onboarding widget for each request parameter:

id[i].integrationContext - Customer's integration context (format: urn:li:organization:{id})
id[i].integrationType - Integration type from the plugin
id[i].tenantType - Tenant type from the plugin
id[i].dataProvider - Use "ATS"

Rows.Text: This is the customer-facing name for the integration.

Blocks.Text: The following example shows how to sync a customer integration with the integration name.

Authorization: Bearer {token}
x-restli-method: batch_partial_update
A successful request will return a 200 OK response code, and you will find the status of each entity in the response body.
Note
Check the response for error statuses corresponding to individual entities you submit.
